question: Which of the following body fluids is explicitly excluded from the application of standard precautions?
explanation: Standard precautions apply to all body fluids except sweat, regardless of whether it contains visible blood. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: To whom should standard precautions be applied in the clinical setting?

options.C: All patients regardless of their infection status
options.D: Only patients admitted to the surgical ward

explanation: Standard precautions are minimum infection control practices that apply to all patient care regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: Standard precautions primarily function by interrupting which part of the chain of infection?

options.C: The genetic makeup of the pathogen

explanation: Standard precautions function primarily by blocking the mode of transmission and protecting portals of entry and exit. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: How many links make up the traditional chain of infection model?
explanation: The chain of infection consists of six interdependent links: agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: According to WHO guidelines, how long should a routine hand rub with an alcohol-based sanitizer take?
explanation: Alcohol-based hand rubs should take 20 to 30 seconds to perform correctly. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Before taking vital signs on a stable patient
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
options.C: Every time you enter a patient room

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water must be performed when hands are visibly dirty or soiled with blood or body fluids. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the very first item typically removed when doffing personal protective equipment?
explanation: Doffing requires careful removal of gloves first, as they are usually the most contaminated item, followed by other protective gear. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: When should medical examination gloves be changed?

options.A: At the end of an 8-hour shift
options.B: Only when they visibly tear or rip
options.D: Only when moving from a clean room to a dirty utility room

explanation: Gloves must be changed between patients to prevent cross-contamination across different individuals. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is the recommended method if a needle must be recapped after use?

options.C: Biting the cap off with teeth
options.D: Holding the cap with the other hand directly

explanation: If recapping is unavoidable, the safe one-handed scoop technique must be used to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Up to what level should a sharps disposal container be filled before it is safely sealed and replaced?
explanation: Sharps containers should never be overfilled and are typically sealed and replaced when they reach the three-quarters full mark. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: What action should be taken if a patient does not have a tissue when coughing or sneezing?

options.A: Cover the mouth and nose with bare hands
options.B: Cough or sneeze into the inner elbow
options.C: Turn towards the nearest healthcare worker
options.D: Cover the face with a plastic examination glove

explanation: If tissues are unavailable, individuals should cough or sneeze into their inner elbow to prevent contaminating their hands. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: What type of mask is recommended when caring for a patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis?
explanation: N95 or higher respirators are required when providing care for patients with suspected airborne infections like tuberculosis. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: How should non-critical patient care equipment like stethoscopes and blood pressure cuffs be managed between different patients?

options.B: Wiped only at the end of the shift
options.C: Washed with plain water once a week
options.D: Shared directly without cleaning if the patients share a room

explanation: Non-critical patient care equipment must be cleaned and disinfected between patients to prevent fomite-mediated transmission. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for minimizing agitation when handling soiled hospital linen?

options.B: To prevent the dispersal of infectious dust particles and microbes into the air
options.C: To keep the laundry room quiet for patients
options.D: To ensure the laundry detergent dissolves faster

explanation: Minimizing agitation prevents infectious dust particles and microbial aerosols from dispersing into the air. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the immediate first aid action following an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound forcefully to drain out contaminated blood
options.B: Wash the area immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Apply concentrated bleach directly into the puncture wound
options.D: Ignore it if the patient appears healthy

explanation: Puncture wounds and skin exposures should be washed immediately with soap and running water without aggressive squeezing. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h8)

question: What type of solution is typically used to disinfect environmental blood and body fluid spills after organic matter is removed?
explanation: Blood and body fluid spills are disinfected using a suitable chlorine-based solution at the correct concentration. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h8)
